posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
![Image](http://members.shaw.ca/holopix/pics/snakelady.jpg)

Blondie is a former fridge-magnet angel with wings surgically removed by me. Her companion reptile is named "Sid", but is not vicious at all. The usual technique - 4X5 BB-640, 660 nm laser, single beam Denisyuk, TEA preswell - I've lost track of the percentage as I'm always tweaking it. About 12 second exposure at ~100 uW/cm^2. Lighting for pic was an Optiled amber LED.

posts.author: eric343
posts.content_md:
Oh WOW!!!

That's an awesome piece of work!

So bright and clear and deep...

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **eric343:** Oh WOW!!!So bright and clear and deep...

Thanks! But it's not really deep - the sun's only about an inch from the plate and is already a bit fuzzy on replay. Maybe the blurring conveys an illusion of depth? The other objects are almost touching the plate.

Another oddity is that I'm using a diverging beam (8-10 degrees) for recording. This leads to slightly exaggerated perspective - among other things it increases the apparent depth of relatively flat objects like fridge magnets. For some strange reason I like this distortion better than the more faithful results that would be obtained from using a collimated beam.

posts.content_md: Dr. Tom...Just curious about the surgury, were the wings thin netting that would move during exposure? Hope you were kind a gave ample ether

posts.author: Tom B.
posts.content_md:
> **LarryD:** Dr. Tom...Just curious about the surgury, were the wings thin netting that would move during exposure? Hope you were kind a gave ample ether

No, they were thick imitation ceramic plastic composite like the rest of her and required use of a jewellers saw and Dremel to remove. They weren't that bad as wings but kind of dominated the upper half of her body and kept getting in the way when posing with other characters. Her posture is now much improved and her back pains have vanished. I took care to give myself plenty of anaesthetic during the procedure
